# bionic-page

> Turn any web page into a bionic reading page. Five configurable modes, per-site rules, a fully reversible transform, and no network.

A Manifest V3 extension for Chrome and Firefox. The readable text of the page you are on is rewritten so the leading part of each word carries more weight, giving the eye a fixed anchor. Every pass is reversible, nothing is uploaded, and settings live in your own browser.

## Page

Everything is on one page, with a section for each part:

- [Live demo](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-page/#demo): the extension's own transform, compiled into the page and run offline in the browser.
- [Before / after](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-page/#compare-section): the same paragraph, with a divider you can drag between the two versions.
- [Reading modes](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-page/#modes): the five modes — Half, Classic, Vowel anchor, Low distraction, and Custom rule — and what each one emphasizes.
- [How it works](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-page/#how): scan, anchor, restore. One reversible pass over the text nodes.
- [Controls](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-page/#control): the keyboard toggle (Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Y), the popup, the on-page pill, and per-site rules.
- [Safety](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-page/#safe): what the transform never touches, and what it does handle.
- [Numbers](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-page/#numbers): test count, e2e checks, lint result, and measured throughput.
- [Privacy](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-page/#privacy): no network requests, no analytics, no accounts. Settings live only in the browser's own storage, and page text is read locally to emphasize it.
- [Install](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-page/#install): build both targets from one source tree.
- [FAQ](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-page/#faq): licensing, PDFs and canvas apps, whether it breaks sites, performance, iframes, shadow DOM, and browser support.
